value.body: State social welfare and women & child development (WCD) departments run schemes for children, women, older persons, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. Officer posts include district social welfare officer, child development project officer (CDPO, under the ICDS/anganwadi system), probation and protection officers, and supervisors. Recruitment and post names vary by state.

items.label: Who recruits
items.value: State PSCs and department / district notices
items.note: Some posts are filled on contract under central schemes

items.label: Typical eligibility
items.value: Graduation; some posts prefer or need an MSW, sociology or related degree

items.label: Anganwadi centres (ICDS)
items.note: ~13.99 lakh operational as on 31 Dec 2024 per a Rajya Sabha reply, as reported
items.source: M/o Women & Child Development, Poshan Tracker data (PIB), as reported

items.label: Students in MSW (Master of Social Work)
items.note: All years, all modes; a common qualification for welfare posts. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Officer-level posts are usually filled through the state PSC (a combined state services exam or a post-specific exam with a written test and interview). Supervisor and contractual posts — for example under child-protection or ICDS schemes — are often advertised directly by the department or district administration. Read each notice for the required degree.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancies are irregular and depend on each state's recruitment calendar.
Field-heavy work: inspections, beneficiary verification, running homes and scheme delivery.
Contract posts can be an entry point but may not carry the security of regular cadre posts.

value.title: Students enrolled in MSW
value.note: All years of the course, all modes. Shows the pool of social work graduates, not the number of government posts. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.
